extracted.intended_audience: Unemployment Insurance Commission (UIC) Insurance Agents (Agent I/II), Benefit Control Officers (BCOs), and district supervisors involved in benefit adjudication, investigation and control
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for processing, deciding, monitoring and investigating unemployment insurance claims, including job-referral, active job search oversight, sickness/maternity benefit handling, decision communication, and benefit-control investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of the application
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is the slightest doubt about the circumstances surrounding the loss of employment, the Agent II first questions the claimant on this point. If the claimant and his former employer contradict each other on this point, the Agent contacts the employer by telephone or by mail after obtaining the claimant's version. Like all relevant information obtained by Agents in the course of their inquiries, the statements of the claimant and the employer are written down and entered on the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Agent II suspects fraud through falsification of reasons for termination, he requests the Benefit Control Unit to investigate. Record all relevant statements in the file; obtain corroboration from employer when contradictions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling voluntary quitting
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimant has left his employment voluntarily, the Agent II must question the claimant in an attempt to determine whether he was in any way justified in quitting his job.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent may vary the length of disqualification depending on seriousness of reasons or presence of extenuating circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessing claimant availability
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the availability of the claimant, the Agent tries to find out the extent to which the claimant's desire to find work is denied by his own restrictions as to the type of employment, the hours and place of work or pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claimants who place unduly restrictive conditions on the type of work they will look for are no longer considered available. Relate this to the 'reasonable interval' and sec.40(3) requiring broadening of suitable employment after that interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Job referral and consequences of refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II can mention available CMC jobs to a claimant and suggest visiting the CMC for an interview; a refusal to follow this advice constitutes grounds for disqualification (sec.40{c}) or even disentitlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision on the claim may be left pending until the CMC notifies the Agent of the placement attempt results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide labour-market advice (sec.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II is required by the provisions of sec.106 of the Act to provide the claimant with such advice and information as his knowledge of the labour market in the region may enable him to give.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide practical advice based on regional labour-market knowledge to assist claimants' job search and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active Job Search Program enrollment and statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent I may hand the claimant an 'active job search statement' to complete and return in two weeks when claimant meets program conditions (possession of job skills in demand).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program is used to review availability; selected occupational categories are determined by a local committee using labour-market data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of occupational categories for Active Job Search
rubrics_metrics.description: An Active Job Search Committee examines statistical and descriptive data from various sources to identify occupational categories for which demand is fairly plentiful and makes claimants in related occupations subject to the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee may also identify claimant groups (age, residence, disabilities) to be systematically included. Occupational coding supports targeted mailing and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, coding and reminders for job-search statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a numerical code to each occupation on application receipt to obtain lists from the computer; send statement form accompanied by form letter reminding obligation to look for work and explaining how to complete the form. Periodic reminder notices are sent with benefit cheques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coding and mailing to ensure coverage and prompt claimants to return statements; include instructions and warnings about risk of losing benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up after non-response to active job-search statement
rubrics_metrics.description: If no reply has been received five days after the end of the period covered by the statement, the Agent II attempts to contact the claimant. If reachable and efforts sufficient, ask for the completed form and advise a second form will be mailed; if unreachable or efforts insufficient, the claimant is disentitled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of disentitlement should remind claimant that entitlement can be regained by demonstrating sufficient efforts and provide new form for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes when statement form is returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Three possible situations: (1) claimant made sufficient efforts — remains entitled and subject to program; (2) claimant discloses new restrictions — either misunderstanding (explain, send second form) or misrepresentation (request Benefit Control Unit investigation); (3) claimant reports insufficient search activity — contact, require office visit, obtain info, and if still inadequate, disentitle as of beginning of period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents should exercise judgment in assessing searches and provide remedial communication where misunderstanding explains restrictions rather than fraud.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for assessing value of job search
rubrics_metrics.description: To assess the value of the search, Agent II is encouraged to take into account 'the number of potential job opportunities in the community within the claimant's occupation, the number of employers, the length of time the claimant has been employed and the manner in which unemployed persons with the claimant's occupation would customarily find re-employment' (Manual, vol.4, sec.437.4.8, p.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use local labour-market context and customary re-employment methods rather than rigid numeric thresholds when judging adequacy of search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation with Medical Adviser for sickness benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Processing sickness benefit applications requires medical knowledge; Agent II retains decision power but must consult the office of the UIC's Medical Adviser at various stages and may be required to initiate an Independent Medical Examination (IME) in defined situations (Manual vol.4, sec.440.5.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IME determines permanence/progress; an IME may not be required if certificate from a specialist is provided or if IME expense is excessive relative to benefit amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent Medical Examination (IME) procedure and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimant required to take an IME is requested to make an appointment with a doctor from a District Office list approved by the Medical Adviser. If claimant does not arrange or keep appointment after one or two weeks, he is disentitled. The examining physician's report provides conclusive proof of the date of recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If doctor finds recovery -> disentitle as of IME day; if doctor does not anticipate recovery before expiry of initial benefit period -> deem entitled until expiry; if doctor anticipates recovery before end -> consult Medical Adviser before decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview at transition from sickness to ordinary benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: After recovery and return to labour market the Agent II must interview claimant to determine ability to work and availability for work; if ability reduced may need to abandon former occupation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview should explain changed obligations, ensure registration with CMC, and consider subjecting claimant to Active Job Search Program if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifying termination circumstances for maternity benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II must clarify circumstances under which employment was terminated for maternity claimants; question both employer and employee to determine whether departure was voluntary or required by employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain occupations (e.g., nurses, waitresses) raise delicate questions. If departure voluntary -> potential disqualification under sec.41. Consider employer policies, collective agreements or legislation regarding priority re-hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement and transition rules for maternity claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If claimant has a guarantee of a job later than the expiration of maternity benefits, she is entitled to ordinary benefits until return. If no guarantee, entitlement to ordinary benefit requires an Agent II interview to verify inability to resume former job and actual availability, paying particular attention to child-care arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pregnancy-related illness prevents return and claimant has not drawn full 15 weeks and produces medical certificate, she may be entitled to sickness benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent responsibilities for arranging transition after maternity (Agent I role)
rubrics_metrics.description: If application was processed by Agent I, he is responsible for contacting claimant shortly after expiration of maternity benefit to arrange transition to ordinary benefit and will invite her for an interview; failure to report for such interview may lead to disentitlement under sec.54(1) and 55(6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interview raises doubts about availability and no guarantee exists, forward file to Agent II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely decision-making and notification (sec.53(3), sec.54(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under sec.53(3) and 54(2) the Agent II is required to examine without delay any applications for benefit that he receives, to make a decision and to notify the claimant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideal is immediate and complete processing of in-person applications, but obtaining clarification from other sources may necessitate short delays; leave claimant aware of outstanding questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to defer decisions and referral powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision may be deferred if Agent II feels it advisable to consult unit supervisor, Supervisor of insurance services, Chief of Operations, regional authorities (especially for labour disputes), or the Medical Adviser. Sec.56 authorizes referral to a Board of referees (rare in practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consultation and referral sparingly and document reasons for deferral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-decision suspicion of false statements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Agent's efforts do not clarify aspects of a case and particularly if he suspects the file contains false statements, he can alert the Benefit Control Unit and ask them to investigate. If doubts arise after an initial decision in applicant's favour, Agent II will hand down another decision suspending payments until further notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend payments pending BCO investigation when credible suspicion of falsification emerges after approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work pace and caseload expectations for Agent II
rubrics_metrics.description: An Agent II is expected to process between forty and sixty files a day, whether he makes a decision or leaves it pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents must balance speed (high throughput) with giving adequate time to unexpected drop-ins and complex cases; ability to handle multiple files simultaneously is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating decisions to claimants (clarity and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: If possible to notify claimant at once, the Agent II must explain the reasons for the decision, remind him of obligations if granted benefit and explain the appeal procedure. Agents often use non-technical language or pamphlets as starting points; some quote the text of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer least technical terms to aid claimant understanding; specify which sections of the Act and Regulations the decision is based on (failure to do so does not invalidate the decision). Avoid swamping claimant with technical terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifying employers when grant affects employer's rights
rubrics_metrics.description: When Record of Employment indicates loss due to misconduct, voluntary quitting, or lay-off during a labour dispute, and Agent II approves the claim, the employer must be notified in good time to enable him to exercise right of appeal under sec.94(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send notice advising employer of decision, his rights and appeal procedure promptly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting explanatory paragraphs and completing decision form
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent II drafts explanatory paragraphs added to form letter to advise claimant of decision, showing how particular criterion of entitlement or grounds for disqualification apply to claimant's situation; must also complete the decision form containing input data for the Regional Payment Centre computer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how criteria apply to facts of case; record structured data for computer implementation of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit control objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The UIC Manual and guidelines establish objectives for benefit control: to identify abuse (detection objective); to encourage compliance by employers and employees (deterrent objective); and to produce savings and revenue to the Unemployment Insurance Account in excess of control costs (self-financing objective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize both financial and legality/ethical rationales; measurement of objectives should account for qualitative effects such as education of citizens and long-term compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefit control scope — legal conditions to check (sec.54(1) and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefit control investigations are intended to establish whether the claimant's situation meets conditions laid down in sec.54(1): meeting general or prior conditions of sec.17; existence of one of the criteria for entitlement under sec.25 (with sec.44 being taken into account in certain cases); and absence of grounds for disqualification under sec.40 or 41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should focus on these statutory elements when assessing continued entitlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: BCO areas of activity (job description)
rubrics_metrics.description: BCO duties include: investigations of specific individual cases (false statements, selected or doubtful claimants), appearance on behalf of the UIC in criminal proceedings, investigations of particular categories of claimants or localities, and maintaining working relationships with other government departments and agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BCOs should combine investigative skills with inter-agency collaboration; be prepared to handle category-wide or regional investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for selecting claimants for investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: BCOs may investigate claimants selected by different methods including statistical/descriptive targeting (e.g., married female claimants 25-35, claimants with minimum insurable weeks), suspicion-based referrals from Agents II, or regional spikes in claimant rolls (e.g., ski resort area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeting should be informed by data patterns and known risk categories while being mindful of fairness and potential profiling concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational supervision and ethics in benefit control
rubrics_metrics.description: Each District Office has a Benefit Control Unit; Sec.501.3.1 stipulates close supervision by the District Manager because of claimant reactions. Hiring practices (ex-policemen, private detectives) have advantages and risks regarding investigative methods and ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise close supervision to prevent overly inquisitorial methods; harmonize roles between BCOs and Insurance Agents to avoid conflict and unethical practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-element post-decision procedure (control, recovery, sanctions)
rubrics_metrics.description: After a decision to grant benefit, the procedure includes benefit control (monitoring continued eligibility), recovery of overpayments (for past improper payments), and sanctions (administrative or criminal) when illegal payments are due to fraudulent activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benefit control may lead to recovery actions or sanctions; BCOs, recovery specialists and legal units coordinate these third-party processes.
